package assignment;

import assignment.piece.Knight;
import assignment.protocol.*;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

public class JesonMor extends Game {
    public JesonMor(Configuration configuration) {
        super(configuration);
    }

    @Override
    public Player start() {
        Player winner = null;
        this.numMoves = 0;
        this.board = configuration.getInitialBoard();
        this.currentPlayer = null;
        this.refreshOutput();

        // Get the list of players in order
        ArrayList<Player> players = new ArrayList<>(configuration.getPlayers());
        int currentPlayerIndex = 0;

        while (true) {
            currentPlayer = players.get(currentPlayerIndex);
            // Get available moves for current player
            Move[] moves = getAvailableMoves(currentPlayer);
            if (moves.length == 0) {
                // No moves available, current player loses, opponent wins
                winner = players.get((currentPlayerIndex + 1) % players.size());
                break;
            }
            // Get next move from player
            Move move = currentPlayer.nextMove(this, moves);
            // Make the move
            movePiece(move);
            // Update score
            Piece movedPiece = board[move.source().x()][move.source().y()];
            updateScore(currentPlayer, movedPiece, move);
            // Refresh output
            this.refreshOutput();
            numMoves++;
            // Check for winner
            winner = getWinner(currentPlayer, movedPiece, move);
            if (winner != null) {
                break;
            }
            // Switch to next player
            currentPlayerIndex = (currentPlayerIndex + 1) % players.size();
        }

        System.out.println();
        System.out.printf("Congratulations! %s%s%s\n", winner.getColor(), winner.getName(), Color.DEFAULT);
        return winner;
    }

    @Override
    public Player getWinner(Player lastPlayer, Piece lastPiece, Move lastMove) {
        // Example logic: if a player has no pieces left, they lose
        // Check if any player has no pieces on the board
        for (Player player : configuration.getPlayers()) {
            boolean hasPiece = false;
            for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
                for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
                    Piece p = board[x][y];
                    if (p != null && p.getOwner().equals(player)) {
                        hasPiece = true;
                        break;
                    }
                }
                if (hasPiece) break;
            }
            if (!hasPiece) {
                // Player has no pieces, they lose, so the other player wins
                for (Player p : configuration.getPlayers()) {
                    if (!p.equals(player)) {
                        return p;
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        // Alternatively, implement specific win conditions here
        return null;
    }

    @Override
    public void updateScore(Player player, Piece piece, Move move) {
        // Calculate Manhattan distance between source and destination
        int distance = Math.abs(move.source().x() - move.destination().x()) +
                       Math.abs(move.source().y() - move.destination().y());
        int newScore = player.getScore() + distance;
        player.setScore(newScore);
    }

    public void movePiece(Move move) {
        Place source = move.source();
        Place destination = move.destination();
        Piece movingPiece = board[source.x()][source.y()];
        // Move the piece
        board[destination.x()][destination.y()] = movingPiece;
        board[source.x()][source.y()] = null;
        // Optionally, update piece's internal position if needed
        // (Assuming Piece has a method to set position, if applicable)
        // movingPiece.setPosition(destination);
    }

    public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
        List<Move> movesList = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
            for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
                Piece piece = board[x][y];
                if (piece != null && piece.getOwner().equals(player)) {
                    Place currentPlace = new Place(x, y);
                    // Get available moves for this piece
                    Move[] pieceMoves = piece.getAvailableMoves(this, currentPlace);
                    for (Move move : pieceMoves) {
                        // Validate move (assuming move is valid as per description)
                        // Additional validation can be added if needed
                        movesList.add(move);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        return movesList.toArray(new Move[0]);
    }

Response Text:---
The `ArcherMoveRule` class implements the `Rule` interface to validate the movement of an Archer piece, which moves similarly to a cannon in Chinese chess. The validation should check if the move is valid according to the rules: moving in a straight line, capturing by jumping over exactly one piece, and moving without capturing if no opponent piece is in the way.

Here's a complete implementation of the `validate` method:

- Check if the move is in a straight line (either same row or same column).
- Count the number of pieces between source and destination.
- If the destination has an opponent's piece, ensure exactly one piece is in between (capture move).
- If the destination is empty, ensure no pieces are in between (normal move).

Below is the complete class with the `validate` method implemented:

```java
package assignment.piece;

import assignment.protocol.Game;
import assignment.protocol.Move;

/**
 * The rule of moving of Archer, which is similar to the moving rule of cannon in Chinese chess.
 *
 * @see <a href='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiangqi#Cannon'>Wikipedia</a>
 */
public class ArcherMoveRule implements Rule {
	@Override
	public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
		if (!(game.getPiece(move.getSource()) instanceof Archer)) {
			return true;
		}

		int srcRow = move.getSource().getRow();
		int srcCol = move.getSource().getCol();
		int destRow = move.getDestination().getRow();
		int destCol = move.getDestination().getCol();

		// Check if move is in a straight line
		if (srcRow != destRow && srcCol != destCol) {
			return false; // Not a straight line
		}

	 int countBetween = 0;

		// Determine direction and count pieces between source and destination
		if (srcRow == destRow) {
			// Horizontal move
			int start = Math.min(srcCol, destCol) + 1;
			int end = Math.max(srcCol, destCol);
			for (int col = start; col < end; col++) {
				if (game.getPieceAt(srcRow, col) != null) {
					countBetween++;
				}
			}
		} else {
			// Vertical move
			int start = Math.min(srcRow, destRow) + 1;
			int end = Math.max(srcRow, destRow);
			for (int row = start; row < end; row++) {
				if (game.getPieceAt(row, srcCol) != null) {
					countBetween++;
				}
			}
		}

		// Check destination piece
		boolean destinationOccupied = game.getPiece(move.getDestination()) != null;
		if (destinationOccupied) {
			// Capture move: must jump over exactly one piece
			return countBetween == 1;
		} else {
			// Normal move: no pieces in between
			return countBetween == 0;
		}
	}

	@Override
	public String getDescription() {
		return "archer move rule is violated";
	}
}
```

**Note:** This implementation assumes that `Game` has a method `getPieceAt(int row, int col)` to access pieces at specific coordinates, which is typical in such game implementations. If not, replace `game.getPieceAt(row, col)` with the appropriate method to access the piece at a specific position.

Response Text:---
The compilation errors indicate that the methods getRow() and getCol() are not defined in the class assignment.protocol.Place, and getPieceAt(int, int) is not a method of the Game interface. Instead, the Game interface likely provides a method getPiece(Position position) to retrieve a piece at a specific position, and the Position class has getRow() and getCol() methods. To fix this, we should use game.getPiece(move.getSource()) and game.getPiece(move.getDestination()) to get the pieces, and use move.getSource() and move.getDestination() directly to access their positions' getRow() and getCol() methods.

Here's the corrected complete Java class:

```java
package assignment.piece;

import assignment.protocol.Game;
import assignment.protocol.Move;

/**
 * The rule of moving of Archer, which is similar to the moving rule of cannon in Chinese chess.
 *
 * @see <a href='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiangqi#Cannon'>Wikipedia</a>
 */
public class ArcherMoveRule implements Rule {
    @Override
    public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
        if (!(game.getPiece(move.getSource()) instanceof Archer)) {
            return true;
        }

        int srcRow = move.getSource().getRow();
        int srcCol = move.getSource().getCol();
        int destRow = move.getDestination().getRow();
        int destCol = move.getDestination().getCol();

        // Check if move is in a straight line
        if (srcRow != destRow && srcCol != destCol) {
            return false; // Not a straight line
        }

        int countBetween = 0;

        // Determine direction and count pieces between source and destination
        if (srcRow == destRow) {
            // Horizontal move
            int start = Math.min(srcCol, destCol) + 1;
            int end = Math.max(srcCol, destCol);
            for (int col = start; col < end; col++) {
                if (game.getPiece(move.getSource().withCol(col)) != null) {
                    countBetween++;
                }
            }
        } else {
            // Vertical move
            int start = Math.min(srcRow, destRow) + 1;
            int end = Math.max(srcRow, destRow);
            for (int row = start; row < end; row++) {
                if (game.getPiece(move.getSource().withRow(row)) != null) {
                    countBetween++;
                }
            }
        }

        // Check destination piece
        boolean destinationOccupied = game.getPiece(move.getDestination()) != null;
        if (destinationOccupied) {
            // Capture move: must jump over exactly one piece
            return countBetween == 1;
        } else {
            // Normal move: no pieces in between
            return countBetween == 0;
        }
    }

    @Override
    public String getDescription() {
        return "archer move rule is violated";
    }
}
```

**Note:** This assumes that the `Position` class has methods `withRow(int row)` and `withCol(int col)` that return a new `Position` with the specified row or column, respectively. If such methods do not exist, you should access the position's row and column directly via public fields or appropriate getters, depending on the actual implementation of the `Position` class.

The compilation errors indicate that the `Place` class in `assignment.protocol` does not have methods `getRow()`, `getCol()`, `withRow(int)`, or `withCol(int)`. To fix this, we should use the methods provided by the `Place` class to access its coordinates and create new `Place` instances with specific coordinates. Typically, such classes have getter methods like `getX()` and `getY()`, or similar, and a constructor or factory method to create new instances.

Assuming the `Place` class has `getX()` and `getY()` methods for coordinates, and a constructor `Place(int x, int y)`, the corrected code will replace `getRow()` with `getX()`, `getCol()` with `getY()`, and use the constructor to create new `Place` objects for the source positions.

Here is the complete corrected Java class:

```java
package assignment.piece;

import assignment.protocol.Game;
import assignment.protocol.Move;
import assignment.protocol.Place;

/**
 * The rule of moving of Archer, which is similar to the moving rule of cannon in Chinese chess.
 *
 * @see <a href='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiangqi#Cannon'>Wikipedia</a>
 */
public class ArcherMoveRule implements Rule {
    @Override
    public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
        if (!(game.getPiece(move.getSource()) instanceof Archer)) {
            return true;
        }

        Place source = move.getSource();
        Place destination = move.getDestination();

        int srcX = source.getX();
        int srcY = source.getY();
        int destX = destination.getX();
        int destY = destination.getY();

        // Check if move is in a straight line
        if (srcX != destX && srcY != destY) {
            return false; // Not a straight line
        }

        int countBetween = 0;

        // Determine direction and count pieces between source and destination
        if (srcX == destX) {
            // Horizontal move
            int startY = Math.min(srcY, destY) + 1;
            int endY = Math.max(srcY, destY);
            for (int y = startY; y < endY; y++) {
                Place checkPlace = new Place(srcX, y);
                if (game.getPiece(checkPlace) != null) {
                    countBetween++;
                }
            }
        } else {
            // Vertical move
            int startX = Math.min(srcX, destX) + 1;
            int endX = Math.max(srcX, destX);
            for (int x = startX; x < endX; x++) {
                Place checkPlace = new Place(x, srcY);
                if (game.getPiece(checkPlace) != null) {
                    countBetween++;
                }
            }
        }

        // Check destination piece
        boolean destinationOccupied = game.getPiece(destination) != null;
        if (destinationOccupied) {
            // Capture move: must jump over exactly one piece
            return countBetween == 1;
        } else {
            // Normal move: no pieces in between
            return countBetween == 0;
        }
    }

    @Override
    public String getDescription() {
        return "archer move rule is violated";
    }
}
```

- Used the `Place(int x, int y)` constructor to create new `Place` instances for checking intermediate positions.  
- Removed the use of non-existent methods `withRow()` and `withCol()`.  

This should resolve the compilation errors and make the code compatible with the `Place` class's actual API.

```java
package assignment.piece;

import assignment.protocol.Game;
import assignment.protocol.Move;

/**
 * Moving rule of Knight in chess (no block)
 */
public class KnightMoveRule implements Rule {

    @Override
    public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
        if (!(game.getPiece(move.getSource()) instanceof Knight)) {
            return true;
        }
        int sourceRow = move.getSource().getRow();
        int sourceCol = move.getSource().getCol();
        int targetRow = move.getTarget().getRow();
        int targetCol = move.getTarget().getCol();

        int rowDiff = Math.abs(targetRow - sourceRow);
        int colDiff = Math.abs(targetCol - sourceCol);

        // Knight moves: (2,1) or (1,2)
        return (rowDiff == 2 && colDiff == 1) || (rowDiff == 1 && colDiff == 2);
    }

    @Override
    public String getDescription() {
        return "knight move rule is violated";
    }
}
```

This implementation correctly checks whether the move is a valid knight move based on the difference in row and column positions.

Response Text:---
The `KnightBlockRule` class implements a rule that checks whether a Knight's move is blocked by another piece, similar to the horse in Chinese chess. To complete the `validate` method, we need to determine if the Knight's move is blocked by a piece located at the "leg" position, which is the position that the Knight "steps over" when moving in an L-shape. 

In Chinese chess, a Knight moves two steps in one direction and then one step perpendicular, but it can be blocked if there's a piece at the intermediate position along its path. The blocking position depends on the move's direction.

Here's the complete implementation:

```java
package assignment.piece;

import assignment.protocol.Game;
import assignment.protocol.Move;
import assignment.protocol.Place;

/**
 * The blocking rule applying on Knights. The rule is similar to the blocking rule for horse in Chinese chess.
 *
 * @see <a href='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiangqi#Horse'>Wikipedia</a>
 */
public class KnightBlockRule implements Rule {
	@Override
	public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
		if (!(game.getPiece(move.getSource()) instanceof Knight)) {
			return true;
		}
		
		Place source = move.getSource();
		Place target = move.getTarget();
		
		int deltaX = target.getX() - source.getX();
		int deltaY = target.getY() - source.getY();
		
		// Determine the intermediate position (the "leg") that must be free
		Place legPosition;
		
		if (Math.abs(deltaX) == 2 && Math.abs(deltaY) == 1) {
			// Moving horizontally then vertically
			int legX = source.getX() + (deltaX / 2);
			int legY = source.getY();
			legPosition = new Place(legX, legY);
		} else if (Math.abs(deltaY) == 2 && Math.abs(deltaX) == 1) {
			// Moving vertically then horizontally
			int legX = source.getX();
			int legY = source.getY() + (deltaY / 2);
			legPosition = new Place(legX, legY);
		} else {
			// Not a valid Knight move
			return false;
		}
		
		// Check if the leg position is occupied
		if (game.getPiece(legPosition) != null) {
			return false; // Move is blocked
		}
		
		return true; // Move is valid if not blocked
	}

	@Override
	public String getDescription() {
		return "knight is blocked by another piece";
	}
}
```

This implementation calculates the "leg" position based on the move's direction and checks if that position is occupied. If it is, the move is invalid due to blocking; otherwise, it is valid.

package assignment.piece;

import assignment.protocol.Game;
import assignment.protocol.Move;
import assignment.protocol.Place;

/**
 * The blocking rule applying on Knights. The rule is similar to the blocking rule for horse in Chinese chess.
 *
 * @see <a href='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiangqi#Horse'>Wikipedia</a>
 */
public class KnightBlockRule implements Rule {
	@Override
	public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
		if (!(game.getPiece(move.getSource()) instanceof Knight)) {
			return true;
		}
		
		Place source = move.getSource();
		Place target = move.getTarget();
		
		int deltaX = target.getX() - source.getX();
		int deltaY = target.getY() - source.getY();
		
		// Determine the intermediate position (the "leg") that must be free
		Place legPosition;
		
		if (Math.abs(deltaX) == 2 && Math.abs(deltaY) == 1) {
			// Moving horizontally then vertically
			int legX = source.getX() + (deltaX / 2);
			int legY = source.getY();
			legPosition = new Place(legX, legY);
		} else if (Math.abs(deltaY) == 2 && Math.abs(deltaX) == 1) {
			// Moving vertically then horizontally
			int legX = source.getX();
			int legY = source.getY() + (deltaY / 2);
			legPosition = new Place(legX, legY);
		} else {
			// Not a valid Knight move
			return false;
		}
		
		// Check if the leg position is occupied
		if (game.getPiece(legPosition) != null) {
			return false; // Move is blocked
		}
		
		return true; // Move is valid if not blocked
	}

	@Override
	public String getDescription() {
		return "knight is blocked by another piece";
	}

package assignment.piece;

import assignment.protocol.Game;
import assignment.protocol.Move;
import assignment.protocol.Place;

/**
 * The blocking rule applying on Knights. The rule is similar to the blocking rule for horse in Chinese chess.
 *
 * @see <a href='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiangqi#Horse'>Wikipedia</a>
 */
public class KnightBlockRule implements Rule {
    @Override
    public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
        if (!(game.getPiece(move.getSource()) instanceof Knight)) {
            return true;
        }

        Place source = move.getSource();
        Place target = move.getDestination();

        int deltaX = target.getX() - source.getX();
        int deltaY = target.getY() - source.getY();

        // Determine the intermediate position (the "leg") that must be free
        Place legPosition;

        if (Math.abs(deltaX) == 2 && Math.abs(deltaY) == 1) {
            // Moving horizontally then vertically
            int legX = source.getX() + (deltaX / 2);
            int legY = source.getY();
            legPosition = new Place(legX, legY);
        } else if (Math.abs(deltaY) == 2 && Math.abs(deltaX) == 1) {
            // Moving vertically then horizontally
            int legX = source.getX();
            int legY = source.getY() + (deltaY / 2);
            legPosition = new Place(legX, legY);
        } else {
            // Not a valid Knight move
            return false;
        }

        // Check if the leg position is occupied
        if (game.getPiece(legPosition) != null) {
            return false; // Move is blocked
        }

        return true; // Move is valid if not blocked
    }

    @Override
    public String getDescription() {
        return "knight is blocked by another piece";
    }
}

Response Text:---
The `VacantRule` class is intended to validate that the source position of a move contains a piece before allowing the move. To implement this, the `validate` method should check whether the game state at the move's source position has a piece. Assuming the `Game` class provides a method to get the piece at a specific position, and the `Move` class provides source position information, the implementation will verify that the source position is not empty.

Here's a complete implementation assuming typical method signatures:

```java
package assignment.piece;

import assignment.protocol.Game;
import assignment.protocol.Move;

/**
 * Global rule that requires the source place of a move must have a piece on it.
 */
public class VacantRule implements Rule {
	@Override
	public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
		// Check if the source position has a piece
		return game.getPieceAt(move.getSource()) != null;
	}

	@Override
	public String getDescription() {
		return "the source of move should have a piece";
	}
}
```

**Note:** This implementation assumes that:
- `Game` has a method `getPieceAt(Position position)` that returns a piece object or null if empty.
- `Move` has a method `getSource()` that returns the position of the move's source.

If the actual method names differ, adjust accordingly.

package assignment.piece;

import assignment.protocol.Game;
import assignment.protocol.Move;

/**
 * Global rule that requires the source place of a move must have a piece on it.

public class VacantRule implements Rule {
    @Override

        return game.getPiece(move.getSource()) != null;

}

```java
package assignment.piece;

import assignment.protocol.Game;
import assignment.protocol.Move;
import assignment.protocol.Piece;

/**
 * Global rule that requires that a piece should not go to a destination where there is another piece belonging to the
 * same player.
 */
public class OccupiedRule implements Rule {
    @Override
    public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
        Piece destinationPiece = game.getPieceAt(move.getDestination());
        if (destinationPiece == null) {
            // Destination is empty, move is valid
            return true;
        }
        // Check if the piece at destination belongs to the same player
        return !destinationPiece.getPlayer().equals(game.getPieceAt(move.getSource()).getPlayer());
    }

    @Override
    public String getDescription() {
        return "piece cannot be captured by another piece belonging to the same player";
    }
}
```

- `Game` has a method `getPieceAt(Position position)` returning a `Piece` or `null` if empty.

Response Text:---
This class represents a Knight piece in a chess-like game, extending the Piece class. The getAvailableMoves method needs to generate all potential moves based on the knight's movement rules, validate each move, and return only the valid ones.

Here's a complete implementation of the Knight class with the getAvailableMoves method fully implemented:

```java
package assignment.piece;

import assignment.protocol.Game;
import assignment.protocol.Move;
import assignment.protocol.Piece;
import assignment.protocol.Place;
import assignment.protocol.Player;

import java.util.ArrayList;

/**
 * Knight piece that moves similar to knight in chess.
 * Rules of move of Knight can be found in wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knight_(chess)).
 *
 * @see <a href='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knight_(chess)'>Wikipedia</a>
 */
public class Knight extends Piece {
    public Knight(Player player) {
        super(player);
    }

    @Override
    public char getLabel() {
        return 'K';
    }

    /**
     * Returns an array of moves that are valid given the current place of the piece.
     * Given the {@link Game} object and the {@link Place} that current knight piece locates, this method should
     * return ALL VALID {@link Move}s according to the current {@link Place} of this knight piece.
     * All the returned {@link Move} should have source equal to the source parameter.
     * <p>
     * Hint: you should consider corner cases when the {@link Move} is not valid on the gameboard.
     * Several tests are provided and your implementation should pass them.
     * <p>
     * <strong>Attention: Student should make sure all {@link Move}s returned are valid.</strong>
     *
     * @param game   the game object
     * @param source the current place of the piece
     * @return an array of available moves
     */
    @Override
    public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {
        ArrayList<Move> validMoves = new ArrayList<>();

        int[][] moveOffsets = {
                {2, 1},
                {1, 2},
                {-1, 2},
                {-2, 1},
                {-2, -1},
                {-1, -2},
                {1, -2},
                {2, -1}
        };

        for (int[] offset : moveOffsets) {
            int newRow = source.getRow() + offset[0];
            int newCol = source.getCol() + offset[1];

            Place targetPlace = new Place(newRow, newCol);

            Move move = new Move(source, targetPlace);

            if (validateMove(game, move)) {
                validMoves.add(move);
            }
        }

        return validMoves.toArray(new Move[0]);
    }

    private boolean validateMove(Game game, Move move) {
        var rules = new Rule[] {
                new OutOfBoundaryRule(),
                new OccupiedRule(),
                new VacantRule(),
                new NilMoveRule(),
                new FirstNMovesProtectionRule(game.getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection()),
                new KnightMoveRule(),
                new KnightBlockRule(),
        };
        for (var rule : rules) {
            if (!rule.validate(game, move)) {
                return false;
            }
        }
        return true;
    }
}
```

**Explanation:**
- The method defines all possible knight moves based on standard chess rules.
- For each move offset, it calculates the target position.
- It creates a Move object from the source to the target position.
- It validates each move using the existing validateMove method.
- Valid moves are collected into a list and returned as an array.

This implementation ensures all generated moves are valid according to the game's rules and the current game state.

```java
package assignment.piece;

import assignment.protocol.Game;
import assignment.protocol.Move;
import assignment.protocol.Piece;
import assignment.protocol.Place;
import assignment.protocol.Player;

import java.util.ArrayList;

/**
 * Knight piece that moves similar to knight in chess.
 * Rules of move of Knight can be found in wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knight_(chess)).
 *
 * @see <a href='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knight_(chess)'>Wikipedia</a>
 */
public class Knight extends Piece {
    public Knight(Player player) {
        super(player);
    }

    @Override
    public char getLabel() {
        return 'K';
    }

    /**
     * Returns an array of moves that are valid given the current place of the piece.
     * Given the {@link Game} object and the {@link Place} that current knight piece locates, this method should
     * return ALL VALID {@link Move}s according to the current {@link Place} of this knight piece.
     * All the returned {@link Move} should have source equal to the source parameter.
     * <p>
     * Hint: you should consider corner cases when the {@link Move} is not valid on the gameboard.
     * Several tests are provided and your implementation should pass them.
     * <p>
     * <strong>Attention: Student should make sure all {@link Move}s returned are valid.</strong>
     *
     * @param game   the game object
     * @param source the current place of the piece
     * @return an array of available moves
     */
    @Override
    public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {
        ArrayList<Move> validMoves = new ArrayList<>();

        int[][] moveOffsets = {
                {2, 1},
                {1, 2},
                {-1, 2},
                {-2, 1},
                {-2, -1},
                {-1, -2},
                {1, -2},
                {2, -1}
        };

        for (int[] offset : moveOffsets) {
            int newRow = source.row + offset[0];
            int newCol = source.col + offset[1];

            Place targetPlace = new Place(newRow, newCol);

            Move move = new Move(source, targetPlace);

            if (validateMove(game, move)) {
                validMoves.add(move);
            }
        }

        return validMoves.toArray(new Move[0]);
    }

    private boolean validateMove(Game game, Move move) {
        var rules = new Rule[] {
                new OutOfBoundaryRule(),
                new OccupiedRule(),
                new VacantRule(),
                new NilMoveRule(),
                new FirstNMovesProtectionRule(game.getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection()),
                new KnightMoveRule(),
                new KnightBlockRule(),
        };
        for (var rule : rules) {
            if (!rule.validate(game, move)) {
                return false;
            }
        }
        return true;
    }
}
```

**Note:** If the `Place` class uses different method names like `getRow()` and `getColumn()`, replace `source.row` with `source.getRow()` and `source.col` with `source.getColumn()`.

Response Text:---
The `Archer` class represents a game piece that moves similarly to the cannon in Chinese chess, which can move any number of empty squares along a rank or file and captures by jumping over exactly one piece. To complete the class, especially the `getAvailableMoves` method, we need to generate all valid moves based on this movement pattern, considering the game rules and board boundaries.

Here's a brief explanation of the approach:
- For each of the four directions (up, down, left, right), iterate through the board from the source position.
- For each direction, first move through empty squares until hitting an obstacle or boundary.
- If an obstacle is encountered, check if it can be jumped over (i.e., the next square in the same direction contains an opponent's piece). If so, the move is valid as a capture.
- Continue this process for all directions, collecting all valid moves.

Below is the complete Java class with the `getAvailableMoves` method implemented accordingly:

```java
package assignment.piece;

import assignment.protocol.Game;
import assignment.protocol.Move;
import assignment.protocol.Piece;
import assignment.protocol.Place;
import assignment.protocol.Player;

import java.util.ArrayList;

/**
 * Archer piece that moves similar to cannon in Chinese chess.
 * Rules of move of Archer can be found in wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiangqi#Cannon).
 *
 * @see <a href='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiangqi#Cannon'>Wikipedia</a>
 */
public class Archer extends Piece {
    public Archer(Player player) {
        super(player);
    }

    @Override
    public char getLabel() {
        return 'A';
    }

    /**
     * Returns an array of moves that are valid given the current place of the piece.
     * Given the {@link Game} object and the {@link Place} that current knight piece locates, this method should
     * return ALL VALID {@link Move}s according to the current {@link Place} of this knight piece.
     * All the returned {@link Move} should have source equal to the source parameter.
     * <p>
     * Hint: you should consider corner cases when the {@link Move} is not valid on the gameboard.
     * Several tests are provided and your implementation should pass them.
     * <p>
     * <strong>Attention: Student should make sure all {@link Move}s returned are valid.</strong>
     *
     * @param game   the game object
     * @param source the current place of the piece
     * @return an array of available moves
     */
    @Override
    public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {
        ArrayList<Move> moves = new ArrayList<>();
        int rows = game.getBoard().length;
        int cols = game.getBoard()[0].length;

        int sourceRow = source.getRow();
        int sourceCol = source.getCol();

        // Directions: up, down, left, right
        int[][] directions = {
                {-1, 0}, // up
                {1, 0},  // down
                {0, -1}, // left
                {0, 1}   // right
        };

        for (int[] dir : directions) {
            boolean jumped = false; // indicates if we've jumped over a piece
            int r = sourceRow + dir[0];
            int c = sourceCol + dir[1];

            // Move along the direction until boundary
            while (r >= 0 && r < rows && c >= 0 && c < cols) {
                Place targetPlace = new Place(r, c);
                Piece targetPiece = game.getBoard()[r][c];

                if (!jumped) {
                    // Not yet jumped over a piece
                    if (targetPiece == null) {
                        // Empty square - valid move
                        Move move = new Move(source, targetPlace);
                        if (validateMove(game, move)) {
                            moves.add(move);
                        }
                        r += dir[0];
                        c += dir[1];
                    } else {
                        // Encountered a piece - can jump over if next is valid
                        jumped = true;
                        r += dir[0];
                        c += dir[1];
                    }
                } else {
                    // Already jumped over one piece, now look for capture
                    if (targetPiece != null) {
                        // Can only capture if opponent's piece
                        if (targetPiece.getPlayer() != this.getPlayer()) {
                            Move move = new Move(source, targetPlace);
                            if (validateMove(game, move)) {
                                moves.add(move);
                            }
                        }
                        // Whether captured or not, stop in this direction
                        break;
                    } else {
                        // Empty square after jump - cannot land here
                        r += dir[0];
                        c += dir[1];
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        return moves.toArray(new Move[0]);
    }

    private boolean validateMove(Game game, Move move) {
        var rules = new Rule[] { new OutOfBoundaryRule(), new OccupiedRule(), new VacantRule(), new NilMoveRule(),
                new FirstNMovesProtectionRule(game.getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection()), new ArcherMoveRule(), };
        for (var rule : rules) {
            if (!rule.validate(game, move)) {
                return false;
            }
        }
        return true;
    }
}

package assignment.piece;

import assignment.protocol.Game;
import assignment.protocol.Move;
import assignment.protocol.Piece;
import assignment.protocol.Place;
import assignment.protocol.Player;

/**
 * Archer piece that moves similar to cannon in Chinese chess.
 * Rules of move of Archer can be found in wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiangqi#Cannon).
 *
 * @see <a href='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiangqi#Cannon'>Wikipedia</a>
 */
public class Archer extends Piece {
    public Archer(Player player) {
        super(player);
    }

    @Override
    public char getLabel() {
        return 'A';
    }

    /**
     * Returns an array of moves that are valid given the current place of the piece.
     * Given the {@link Game} object and the {@link Place} that current knight piece locates, this method should
     * return ALL VALID {@link Move}s according to the current {@link Place} of this knight piece.
     * All the returned {@link Move}s should have source equal to the source parameter.
     * <p>
     * Hint: you should consider corner cases when the {@link Move} is not valid on the gameboard.
     * Several tests are provided and your implementation should pass them.
     * <p>
     * <strong>Attention: Student should make sure all {@link Move}s returned are valid.</strong>
     *
     * @param game   the game object
     * @param source the current place of the piece
     * @return an array of available moves
     */
    @Override
    public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {
        ArrayList<Move> moves = new ArrayList<>();
        Piece[][] board = game.getBoard(); // Assuming getBoard() returns Piece[][]
        int rows = board.length;
        int cols = board[0].length;

        int sourceRow = source.getRow(); // Assuming getRow() exists
        int sourceCol = source.getCol(); // Assuming getCol() exists

        // Directions: up, down, left, right
        int[][] directions = {
                {-1, 0}, // up
                {1, 0},  // down
                {0, -1}, // left
                {0, 1}   // right
        };

        for (int[] dir : directions) {
            boolean jumped = false; // indicates if we've jumped over a piece
            int r = sourceRow + dir[0];
            int c = sourceCol + dir[1];

            while (r >= 0 && r < rows && c >= 0 && c < cols) {
                Place targetPlace = new Place(r, c);
                Piece targetPiece = board[r][c];

                if (!jumped) {
                    // Not yet jumped over a piece
                    if (targetPiece == null) {
                        // Empty square - valid move
                        Move move = new Move(source, targetPlace);
                        if (validateMove(game, move)) {
                            moves.add(move);
                        }
                        r += dir[0];
                        c += dir[1];
                    } else {
                        // Encountered a piece - can jump over if next is valid
                        jumped = true;
                        r += dir[0];
                        c += dir[1];
                    }
                } else {
                    // Already jumped over one piece, now look for capture
                    if (targetPiece != null) {
                        // Can only capture if opponent's piece
                        if (targetPiece.getPlayer() != this.getPlayer()) {
                            Move move = new Move(source, targetPlace);
                            if (validateMove(game, move)) {
                                moves.add(move);
                            }
                        }
                        break; // Stop after attempting capture
                    } else {
                        // Empty square after jump - cannot land here
                        r += dir[0];
                        c += dir[1];
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        return moves.toArray(new Move[0]);
    }

    private boolean validateMove(Game game, Move move) {
        var rules = new Rule[] { new OutOfBoundaryRule(), new OccupiedRule(), new VacantRule(), new NilMoveRule(),
                new FirstNMovesProtectionRule(game.getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection()), new ArcherMoveRule(), };
        for (var rule : rules) {
            if (!rule.validate(game, move)) {
                return false;
            }
        }
        return true;
    }
}

package assignment.piece;

import assignment.protocol.Game;
import assignment.protocol.Move;
import assignment.protocol.Piece;
import assignment.protocol.Place;
import assignment.protocol.Player;
import java.util.ArrayList;

/**
 * Archer piece that moves similar to cannon in Chinese chess.
 * Rules of move of Archer can be found in wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiangqi#Cannon).
 *
 * @see <a href='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiangqi#Cannon'>Wikipedia</a>
 */
public class Archer extends Piece {
    public Archer(Player player) {
        super(player);
    }

    @Override
    public char getLabel() {
        return 'A';
    }

    /**
     * Returns an array of moves that are valid given the current place of the piece.
     * Given the {@link Game} object and the {@link Place} that current knight piece locates, this method should
     * return ALL VALID {@link Move}s according to the current {@link Place} of this knight piece.
     * All the returned {@link Move}s should have source equal to the source parameter.
     * <p>
     * Hint: you should consider corner cases when the {@link Move} is not valid on the gameboard.
     * Several tests are provided and your implementation should pass them.
     * <p>
     * <strong>Attention: Student should make sure all {@link Move}s returned are valid.</strong>
     *
     * @param game   the game object
     * @param source the current place of the piece
     * @return an array of available moves
     */
    @Override
    public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {
        ArrayList<Move> moves = new ArrayList<>();
        Piece[][] board = game.getBoard(); // Assuming getBoard() returns Piece[][]
        int rows = board.length;
        int cols = board[0].length;

        int sourceRow = source.getRow(); // Assuming getRow() exists
        int sourceCol = source.getCol(); // Assuming getCol() exists

        // Directions: up, down, left, right
        int[][] directions = {
                {-1, 0}, // up
                {1, 0},  // down
                {0, -1}, // left
                {0, 1}   // right
        };

        for (int[] dir : directions) {
            boolean jumped = false; // indicates if we've jumped over a piece
            int r = sourceRow + dir[0];
            int c = sourceCol + dir[1];

            while (r >= 0 && r < rows && c >= 0 && c < cols) {
                Place targetPlace = new Place(r, c);
                Piece targetPiece = board[r][c];

                if (!jumped) {
                    // Not yet jumped over a piece
                    if (targetPiece == null) {
                        // Empty square - valid move
                        Move move = new Move(source, targetPlace);
                        if (validateMove(game, move)) {
                            moves.add(move);
                        }
                        r += dir[0];
                        c += dir[1];
                    } else {
                        // Encountered a piece - can jump over if next is valid
                        jumped = true;
                        r += dir[0];
                        c += dir[1];
                    }
                } else {
                    // Already jumped over one piece, now look for capture
                    if (targetPiece != null) {
                        // Can only capture if opponent's piece
                        if (targetPiece.getPlayer() != this.getPlayer()) {
                            Move move = new Move(source, targetPlace);
                            if (validateMove(game, move)) {
                                moves.add(move);
                            }
                        }
                        break; // Stop after attempting capture
                    } else {
                        // Empty square after jump - cannot land here
                        r += dir[0];
                        c += dir[1];
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        return moves.toArray(new Move[0]);
    }

    private boolean validateMove(Game game, Move move) {
        var rules = new Rule[] { new OutOfBoundaryRule(), new OccupiedRule(), new VacantRule(), new NilMoveRule(),
                new FirstNMovesProtectionRule(game.getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection()), new ArcherMoveRule(), };
        for (var rule : rules) {
            if (!rule.validate(game, move)) {
                return false;
            }
        }
        return true;
    }
}

import assignment.protocol.Move;
import assignment.protocol.Piece;
import assignment.protocol.Place;
import assignment.protocol.Player;
import java.util.ArrayList;

/**
 * Archer piece that moves similar to cannon in Chinese chess.
 * Rules of move of Archer can be found in wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiangqi#Cannon).
 *
 * @see <a href='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiangqi#Cannon'>Wikipedia</a>
 */
public class Archer extends Piece {
    public Archer(Player player) {
        super(player);
    }

    @Override
    public char getLabel() {
        return 'A';
    }

    /**
     * Returns an array of moves that are valid given the current place of the piece.
     * Given the {@link Game} object and the {@link Place} that current knight piece locates, this method should
     * return ALL VALID {@link Move}s according to the current {@link Place} of this knight piece.
     * All the returned {@link Move}s should have source equal to the source parameter.
     * <p>
     * Hint: you should consider corner cases when the {@link Move} is not valid on the gameboard.
     * Several tests are provided and your implementation should pass them.
     * <p>
     * <strong>Attention: Student should make sure all {@link Move}s returned are valid.</strong>
     *
     * @param game   the game object
     * @param source the current place of the piece
     * @return an array of available moves
     */
    @Override
    public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {
        ArrayList<Move> moves = new ArrayList<>();
        Piece[][] board = game.getBoard(); // Access the game board
        int rows = board.length;
        int cols = board[0].length;

        int sourceRow = source.getRow(); // Access source row
        int sourceCol = source.getCol(); // Access source column

        // Directions: up, down, left, right
        int[][] directions = {
                {-1, 0}, // up
                {1, 0},  // down
                {0, -1}, // left
                {0, 1}   // right
        };

        for (int[] dir : directions) {
            boolean jumped = false; // indicates if we've jumped over a piece
            int r = sourceRow + dir[0];
            int c = sourceCol + dir[1];

            while (r >= 0 && r < rows && c >= 0 && c < cols) {
                Place targetPlace = new Place(r, c);
                Piece targetPiece = board[r][c];

                if (!jumped) {
                    // Not yet jumped over a piece
                    if (targetPiece == null) {
                        // Empty square - valid move
                        Move move = new Move(source, targetPlace);
                        if (validateMove(game, move)) {
                            moves.add(move);
                        }
                        r += dir[0];
                        c += dir[1];
                    } else {
                        // Encountered a piece - can jump over if next is valid
                        jumped = true;
                        r += dir[0];
                        c += dir[1];
                    }
                } else {
                    // Already jumped over one piece, now look for capture
                    if (targetPiece != null) {
                        // Can only capture if opponent's piece
                        if (targetPiece.getPlayer() != this.getPlayer()) {
                            Move move = new Move(source, targetPlace);
                            if (validateMove(game, move)) {
                                moves.add(move);
                            }
                        }
                        break; // Stop after attempting capture
                    } else {
                        // Empty square after jump - cannot land here
                        r += dir[0];
                        c += dir[1];
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        return moves.toArray(new Move[0]);
    }

    private boolean validateMove(Game game, Move move) {
        var rules = new Rule[] { new OutOfBoundaryRule(), new OccupiedRule(), new VacantRule(), new NilMoveRule(),
                new FirstNMovesProtectionRule(game.getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection()), new ArcherMoveRule(), };
        for (var rule : rules) {
            if (!rule.validate(game, move)) {
                return false;
            }
        }
        return true;
    }
}

package assignment.piece;

import assignment.protocol.Game;
import assignment.protocol.Move;

/**
 * The rule that requires capturing piece is not allowed within the first certain number of moves.
 */
public class FirstNMovesProtectionRule implements Rule {
	/**
	 * The number of moves within which capturing piece is not allowed.
	 */
	private final int numProtectedMoves;

	public FirstNMovesProtectionRule(int numProtectedMoves) {
		this.numProtectedMoves = numProtectedMoves;
	}

	@Override
	public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
		// Check if the move is a capture
		if (move.isCapture()) {
			// Check if the current move count is within the protected range
			int moveCount = game.getMoveCount();
			if (moveCount <= this.numProtectedMoves) {
				return false; // Move is invalid as it captures within protected moves
			}
		}
		return true; // Move is valid if not a capture or outside protected range
	}

	@Override
	public String getDescription() {
		return "Capturing piece in the first " + this.numProtectedMoves + " moves are not allowed";
	}
}
```

**Note:** This implementation assumes that `Game` has a method `getMoveCount()` returning an integer representing the total number of moves played, and `Move` has a method `isCapture()` returning a boolean indicating if the move captures a piece. If these methods differ, adjust accordingly.

The errors indicate that the move validation logic in your game is failing, likely because the `validate` method in `NilMoveRule` is returning `false` when the source and destination are different, which is the opposite of the intended behavior. The current implementation returns `!move.getSource().equals(move.getDestination())`, which is correct logically, but the test failures suggest that the move validation is not functioning as expected elsewhere, possibly due to how `Move` objects or their positions are compared.

**Most probable cause:** The `equals` method on the position objects (probably `Position` or similar) used in `Move` is not overridden, so `equals` defaults to reference equality. This causes two different position objects with the same coordinates to be considered unequal, leading to incorrect validation results.

**Solution:** Override the `equals` and `hashCode` methods in the `Position` class (or equivalent class used for move sources and destinations) to ensure value-based comparison. This will make `move.getSource().equals(move.getDestination())` correctly identify when positions are the same or different.

---

### Complete `Position` class with `equals` and `hashCode` overridden:

```java
package assignment.protocol;

import java.util.Objects;

/**
 * Represents a position on the game board.
 */
public class Position {
    private final int x;
    private final int y;

    public Position(int x, int y) {
        this.x = x;
        this.y = y;
    }

    public int getX() {
        return x;
    }

    public int getY() {
        return y;
    }

    @Override
    public boolean equals(Object o) {
        if (this == o) return true;
        if (!(o instanceof Position)) return false;
        Position position = (Position) o;
        return x == position.x && y == position.y;
    }

    @Override
    public int hashCode() {
        return Objects.hash(x, y);
    }
}
```

**Note:** If your project already has a `Position` class, ensure it has proper `equals` and `hashCode` implementations as shown. This change will fix the move validation logic and resolve the test failures related to move validation and move availability checks.

Response Text:---
The `OutOfBoundaryRule` class is meant to validate whether the source and destination positions of a move are within the boundaries of the game board. To complete this class, we need to implement the `validate` method to check if both the source and destination coordinates are within the valid range of the game board, which is typically defined by the `Game` interface or class.

Assuming the `Game` interface provides methods like `getBoardWidth()` and `getBoardHeight()` to retrieve the dimensions of the game board, and the `Move` class provides methods like `getSource()` and `getDestination()` that return coordinate objects with `getX()` and `getY()` methods, the implementation can be as follows:

```java
package assignment.piece;

import assignment.protocol.Game;
import assignment.protocol.Move;

/**
 * Global rule that requires the source and destination should be inside the board boundary.
 */
public class OutOfBoundaryRule implements Rule {
	@Override
	public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
		// Get board dimensions
		int width = game.getBoardWidth();
		int height = game.getBoardHeight();

		// Get source and destination coordinates
		var source = move.getSource();
		var destination = move.getDestination();

		// Check if source is within boundaries
		boolean sourceInBounds = source.getX() >= 0 && source.getX() < width
				&& source.getY() >= 0 && source.getY() < height;

		// Check if destination is within boundaries
		boolean destinationInBounds = destination.getX() >= 0 && destination.getX() < width
				&& destination.getY() >= 0 && destination.getY() < height;

		// Return true if both source and destination are within boundaries
		return sourceInBounds && destinationInBounds;
	}

	@Override
	public String getDescription() {
		return "place is out of boundary of gameboard";
	}
}
```

This implementation ensures that both the source and destination coordinates are within the game board's boundaries, fulfilling the validation rule.

/**

                && source.getY() >= 0 && source.getY() < height;

        // Check if destination is within boundaries

                && destination.getY() >= 0 && destination.getY() < height;

        // Return true if both source and destination are within boundaries

Response Text:---
The `RandomPlayer` class extends `Player` and is designed to select a move randomly from the available options. The `nextMove` method currently returns the first move, but it should select a move at random to fulfill its purpose.

Here's the complete implementation with the `nextMove` method properly randomized:

```java
package assignment.player;

import assignment.protocol.Game;
import assignment.protocol.Color;
import assignment.protocol.Move;
import assignment.protocol.Player;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;

import java.util.Random;

/**
 * A computer player that makes a move randomly.
 */
public class RandomPlayer extends Player {
    private final Random random;

    public RandomPlayer(String name, Color color) {
        super(name, color);
        this.random = new Random();
    }

    public RandomPlayer(String name) {
        this(name, Color.BLUE);
    }

    /**
     * Choose a move from available moves.
     * This method will be called by {@link Game} object to get the move that the player wants to make when it is the
     * player's turn.
     * <p>
     * {@link RandomPlayer} chooses a move from available ones randomly.
     * <p>
     * <strong>Attention: Student should make sure the {@link Move} returned is valid.</strong>
     *
     * @param game           the current game object
     * @param availableMoves available moves for this player to choose from.
     * @return the chosen move
     */
    @Override
    public Move nextMove(Game game, Move[] availableMoves) {
        int index = random.nextInt(availableMoves.length);
        return availableMoves[index];
    }
}
```

**Explanation:**
- Added a `Random` instance as a class member for better performance.
- In `nextMove`, selected a random index within the bounds of `availableMoves`.
- Returned the move at the randomly selected index, ensuring a valid move is chosen randomly.

	 * Note that in the {@link Game}.board, the index starts from 0 in both x and y dimension, while in the console

	private String validateMove(Game game, Move move) {
		var rules = new Rule[] { new OutOfBoundaryRule(), new OccupiedRule(), new VacantRule(), new NilMoveRule(),
				new FirstNMovesProtectionRule(game.getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection()), new ArcherMoveRule(),
				new KnightMoveRule(), new KnightBlockRule(), };
		for (var rule : rules) {
			if (!rule.validate(game, move)) {
				return rule.getDescription();
			}

			var piece = game.getPiece(move.getSource());
			if (piece == null) {
				return "No piece at " + move.getSource().toString();
			}
			if (!this.equals(piece.getPlayer())) {
				return "Cannot move a piece not belonging to you";
			}
		}
		return null;
	}

	private static Place parsePlace(String str) {
		if (str.length() < 2) {
			return null;
		}
		try {
			var x = str.charAt(0) - 'a';
			var y = Integer.parseInt(str.substring(1)) - 1;
			return new Place(x, y);
		} catch (NumberFormatException e) {
			return null;
		}
	}

	private static Move parseMove(String str) {
		var segments = str.split("->");
		if (segments.length < 2) {
			return null;
		}
		var source = parsePlace(segments[0].strip());
		if (source == null) {
			return null;
		}
		var destination = parsePlace(segments[1].strip());
		if (destination == null) {
			return null;
		}
		return new Move(source, destination);
	}

Response Text:---
The `ConsolePlayer` class is designed to allow a human player to input moves via the console. The key method to implement is `nextMove`, which prompts the user for input, validates it, and returns a valid move from the list of available moves.

Here's a complete implementation of the class with the `nextMove` method fully implemented:

```java
package assignment.player;

import assignment.protocol.Game;
import assignment.piece.*;
import assignment.protocol.Color;
import assignment.protocol.Move;
import assignment.protocol.Place;
import assignment.protocol.Player;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;

import java.util.Scanner;

/**
 * The player that makes move according to user input from console.
 */
public class ConsolePlayer extends Player {
    private final Scanner scanner;

    public ConsolePlayer(String name, Color color) {
        super(name, color);
        this.scanner = new Scanner(System.in);
    }

    public ConsolePlayer(String name) {
        this(name, Color.GREEN);
    }

    /**
     * Choose a move from available moves.
     * This method will be called by {@link Game} object to get the move that the player wants to make when it is the
     * player's turn.
     * <p>
     * {@link ConsolePlayer} returns a move according to user's input in the console.
     * The console input format should conform the format described in the assignment description.
     * (e.g. {@literal a1->b3} means move the {@link Piece} at {@link Place}(x=0,y=0) to {@link Place}(x=1,y=2))
     * Note that in the {@link Game}.board, the index starts from 0 in both x and y dimension, while in the console
     * display, x dimension index starts from 'a' and y dimension index starts from 1.
     * <p>
     * Hint: be sure to handle invalid input to avoid invalid {@link Move}s.
     * <p>
     * <strong>Attention: Student should make sure the {@link Move} returned is valid.</strong>
     * <p>
     * <strong>Attention: {@link Place} object uses integer as index of x and y-axis, both starting from 0 to
     * facilitate programming.</strong>
     *
     * @param game           the current game object
     * @param availableMoves available moves for this player to choose from.
     * @return the chosen move
     */
    @Override
    public Move nextMove(Game game, Move[] availableMoves) {
        while (true) {
            System.out.println("Enter your move (e.g., a1->b3): ");
            String input = scanner.nextLine().trim();

            Move move = parseMove(input);
            if (move == null) {
                System.out.println("Invalid format. Please try again.");
                continue;
            }

            // Check if move is in availableMoves
            boolean isValidMove = false;
            for (Move m : availableMoves) {
                if (m.equals(move)) {
                    isValidMove = true;
                    move = m; // Use the actual move object from availableMoves
                    break;
                }
            }
            if (!isValidMove) {
                System.out.println("Move not available. Please select a valid move.");
                continue;
            }

            // Optionally, validate move with game rules
            String validationError = validateMove(game, move);
            if (validationError != null) {
                System.out.println("Invalid move: " + validationError);
                continue;
            }

            return move;
        }
    }

    private String validateMove(Game game, Move move) {
        var rules = new assignment.player.Rule[] {
            new assignment.player.OutOfBoundaryRule(),
            new assignment.player.OccupiedRule(),
            new assignment.player.VacantRule(),
            new assignment.player.NilMoveRule(),
            new assignment.player.FirstNMovesProtectionRule(game.getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection()),
            new assignment.player.ArcherMoveRule(),
            new assignment.player.KnightMoveRule(),
            new assignment.player.KnightBlockRule()
        };
        for (var rule : rules) {
            if (!rule.validate(game, move)) {
                return rule.getDescription();
            }
        }
        var piece = game.getPiece(move.getSource());
        if (piece == null) {
            return "No piece at " + move.getSource().toString();
        }
        if (!this.equals(piece.getPlayer())) {
            return "Cannot move a piece not belonging to you";
        }
        return null;
    }

    private static Place parsePlace(String str) {
        if (str.length() < 2) {
            return null;
        }
        try {
            char colChar = str.charAt(0);
            if (colChar < 'a' || colChar > 'z') {
                return null;
            }
            int x = colChar - 'a';

            String rowStr = str.substring(1).trim();
            int y = Integer.parseInt(rowStr) - 1;

            return new Place(x, y);
        } catch (NumberFormatException e) {
            return null;
        }
    }

    private static Move parseMove(String str) {
        String[] segments = str.split("->");
        if (segments.length != 2) {
            return null;
        }
        Place source = parsePlace(segments[0].trim());
        Place destination = parsePlace(segments[1].trim());
        if (source == null || destination == null) {
            return null;
        }
        return new Move(source, destination);
    }
}
```

**Explanation:**
- The constructor initializes a `Scanner` for reading console input.
- The `nextMove` method prompts the user, reads input, and parses it into a `Move`.
- It checks if the move is among the available moves.
- It validates the move against game rules.
- If valid, it returns the move; otherwise, it prompts again.
- Helper methods `parsePlace` and `parseMove` convert string input into `Place` and `Move` objects, handling invalid formats gracefully.

This implementation ensures robust user input handling and move validation, enabling the console-based player to participate correctly in the game.

				new KnightMoveRule(), new KnightBlockRule(), };

				return "No piece at " + move.getSource().toString();

			if (!this.equals(piece.getPlayer())) {
				return "Cannot move a piece not belonging to you";
			}
		}
		return null;
	}

	private static Place parsePlace(String str) {
		if (str.length() < 2) {
			return null;
		}
		try {
			var x = str.charAt(0) - 'a';
			var y = Integer.parseInt(str.substring(1)) - 1;
			return new Place(x, y);
		} catch (NumberFormatException e) {
			return null;
		}
	}

		if (segments.length < 2) {
			return null;
		}
		var source = parsePlace(segments[0].strip());
		if (source == null) {
			return null;
		}
		var destination = parsePlace(segments[1].strip());
		if (destination == null) {
			return null;
		}

/**

public class ConsolePlayer extends Player {
    private final Scanner scanner;

    public ConsolePlayer(String name, Color color) {
        super(name, color);
        this.scanner = new Scanner(System.in);

    public ConsolePlayer(String name) {

    }

    /**
     * Choose a move from available moves.
     * This method will be called by {@link Game} object to get the move that the player wants to make when it is the
     * player's turn.
     * <p>
     * {@link ConsolePlayer} returns a move according to user's input in the console.
     * The console input format should conform the format described in the assignment description.
     * (e.g. {@literal a1->b3} means move the {@link Piece} at {@link Place}(x=0,y=0) to {@link Place}(x=1,y=2))
     * Note that in the {@link Game}.board, the index starts from 0 in both x and y dimension, while in the console
     * display, x dimension index starts from 'a' and y dimension index starts from 1.
     * <p>
     * Hint: be sure to handle invalid input to avoid invalid {@link Move}s.
     * <p>
     * <strong>Attention: Student should make sure the {@link Move} returned is valid.</strong>
     * <p>
     * <strong>Attention: {@link Place} object uses integer as index of x and y-axis, both starting from 0 to
     * facilitate programming.</strong>
     *
     * @param game           the current game object
     * @param availableMoves available moves for this player to choose from.
     * @return the chosen move
     */
    @Override
    public Move nextMove(Game game, Move[] availableMoves) {
        while (true) {
            System.out.println("Enter your move (e.g., a1->b3): ");
            String input = scanner.nextLine().trim();

            Move move = parseMove(input);
            if (move == null) {
                System.out.println("Invalid format. Please try again.");
                continue;
            }

            // Check if move is in availableMoves
            boolean isValidMove = false;
            for (Move m : availableMoves) {
                if (m.equals(move)) {
                    isValidMove = true;
                    move = m; // Use the actual move object from availableMoves
                    break;
                }
            }
            if (!isValidMove) {
                System.out.println("Move not available. Please select a valid move.");
                continue;
            }

            // Optionally, validate move with game rules
            String validationError = validateMove(game, move);
            if (validationError != null) {
                System.out.println("Invalid move: " + validationError);
                continue;
            }

            return move;
        }
    }

    private String validateMove(Game game, Move move) {
        var rules = new assignment.player.Rule[] {
            new assignment.player.OutOfBoundaryRule(),
            new assignment.player.OccupiedRule(),
            new assignment.player.VacantRule(),
            new assignment.player.NilMoveRule(),
            new assignment.player.FirstNMovesProtectionRule(game.getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection()),
            new assignment.player.ArcherMoveRule(),
            new assignment.player.KnightMoveRule(),
            new assignment.player.KnightBlockRule()
        };
        for (var rule : rules) {
            if (!rule.validate(game, move)) {
                return rule.getDescription();
            }
        }
        var piece = game.getPiece(move.getSource());
        if (piece == null) {
            return "No piece at " + move.getSource().toString();
        }
        if (!this.equals(piece.getPlayer())) {
            return "Cannot move a piece not belonging to you";
        }
        return null;
    }

    private static Place parsePlace(String str) {
        if (str.length() < 2) {
            return null;
        }
        try {
            char colChar = str.charAt(0);
            if (colChar < 'a' || colChar > 'z') {
                return null;
            }
            int x = colChar - 'a';

            String rowStr = str.substring(1).trim();
            int y = Integer.parseInt(rowStr) - 1;

            return new Place(x, y);
        } catch (NumberFormatException e) {
            return null;
        }
    }

    private static Move parseMove(String str) {
        String[] segments = str.split("->");
        if (segments.length != 2) {
            return null;
        }
        Place source = parsePlace(segments[0].trim());
        Place destination = parsePlace(segments[1].trim());
        if (source == null || destination == null) {
            return null;
        }
        return new Move(source, destination);
    }

            boolean isValidMove = false;
            for (Move m : availableMoves) {
                if (m.equals(move)) {
                    isValidMove = true;

                    break;
                }
            }
            if (!isValidMove) {
                System.out.println("Move not available. Please select a valid move.");
                continue;
            }

            // Optionally, validate move with game rules
            String validationError = validateMove(game, move);
            if (validationError != null) {
                System.out.println("Invalid move: " + validationError);
                continue;
            }

            return move;
        }
    }

    private String validateMove(Game game, Move move) {
        var rules = new assignment.player.Rule[] {
            new assignment.player.OutOfBoundaryRule(),
            new assignment.player.OccupiedRule(),
            new assignment.player.VacantRule(),
            new assignment.player.NilMoveRule(),

            return new Place(x, y);

            return null;

     * The console input format should conform the format described in the assignment description.
     * (e.g. {@literal a1->b3} means move the {@link Piece} at {@link Place}(x=0,y=0) to {@link Place}(x=1,y=2))
     * Note that in the {@link Game}.board, the index starts from 0 in both x and y dimension, while in the console
     * display, x dimension index starts from 'a' and y dimension index starts from 1.
     * <p>
     * Hint: be sure to handle invalid input to avoid invalid {@link Move}s.
     * <p>
     * <strong>Attention: Student should make sure the {@link Move} returned is valid.</strong>
     * <p>
     * <strong>Attention: {@link Place} object uses integer as index of x and y-axis, both starting from 0 to
     * facilitate programming.</strong>
     *
     * @param game           the current game object
     * @param availableMoves available moves for this player to choose from.
     * @return the chosen move
     */
    @Override
    public Move nextMove(Game game, Move[] availableMoves) {
        while (true) {
            System.out.println("Enter your move (e.g., a1->b3): ");
            String input = scanner.nextLine().trim();

            Move move = parseMove(input);
            if (move == null) {
                System.out.println("Invalid format. Please try again.");
                continue;
            }

            // Check if move is in availableMoves
            boolean isValidMove = false;
            for (Move m : availableMoves) {
                if (m.equals(move)) {
                    isValidMove = true;
                    move = m; // Use the actual move object from availableMoves
                    break;
                }
            }
            if (!isValidMove) {
                System.out.println("Move not available. Please select a valid move.");
                continue;
            }

            // Validate move with game rules
            String validationError = validateMove(game, move);
            if (validationError != null) {
                System.out.println("Invalid move: " + validationError);
                continue;
            }

            return move;
        }
    }

    private String validateMove(Game game, Move move) {
        var rules = new Rule[] {
            new OutOfBoundaryRule(),
            new OccupiedRule(),
            new VacantRule(),
            new NilMoveRule(),
            new FirstNMovesProtectionRule(game.getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection()),
            new ArcherMoveRule(),
            new KnightMoveRule(),
            new KnightBlockRule()
        };
        for (var rule : rules) {
            if (!rule.validate(game, move)) {
                return rule.getDescription();
            }
        }
        var piece = game.getPiece(move.getSource());
        if (piece == null) {
            return "No piece at " + move.getSource().toString();
        }
        if (!this.equals(piece.getPlayer())) {
            return "Cannot move a piece not belonging to you";
        }
        return null;
    }

    private static Place parsePlace(String str) {
        if (str.length() < 2) {
            return null;
        }
        try {
            char colChar = str.charAt(0);
            if (colChar < 'a' || colChar > 'z') {
                return null;
            }
            int x = colChar - 'a';

            String rowStr = str.substring(1).trim();
            int y = Integer.parseInt(rowStr) - 1;

            return new Place(x, y);
        } catch (NumberFormatException e) {
            return null;
        }
    }

    private static Move parseMove(String str) {
        String[] segments = str.split("->");
        if (segments.length != 2) {
            return null;
        }
        Place source = parsePlace(segments[0].trim());
        Place destination = parsePlace(segments[1].trim());
        if (source == null || destination == null) {
            return null;
        }
        return new Move(source, destination);
    }
